entry.idea: Restaurants already run security cameras but nobody watches them for sales or theft, so Emilia AI reads that camera footage in real time and turns it into a coach for staff and a fraud watchdog.
entry.lesson: Point AI at data a business already collects passively, like security video, and turn it into an active tool instead of building new sensors.
entry.name: Emilia AI

growth.reason: The only public numbers are the size of this first funding round, with no user, revenue or restaurant-count figures yet.

market.reason: Restaurants are a huge, worldwide industry, but the product is aimed only at that one vertical rather than at every kind of business.

tech.reason: Applying computer vision to existing security cameras for coaching and fraud detection is solid engineering, but video analytics for retail is an active field a strong competitor could match within a year.

entry.twist: It reuses cameras restaurants already own as its sensor, so there is no new hardware to install, and one feed does two jobs: coaching staff to sell more and catching fraud.
entry.who_pays: Restaurant chains and operators who pay a subscription to run the software on their existing camera systems.
entry.why_now: Restaurant margins are thin and staff turnover is high, so cheap, fast AI video analysis that lifts sales and catches theft pays for itself quickly.
